answer: A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit. The ripple of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. The design leans on receipt hashes checked against public logs before trust. Written in a long technical clauses, one short sentence to close register, it stays short. The horizon lists finished tasks with their hashes, and the vine is where a second reviewer recomputes them.
